purpose: Small release-quality visual-redaction subset. This is not the broad discovery corpus: each row names the independent visual evidence and the mutation it must detect.

rows.adjudication: Text must disappear from the target rectangle while surrounding text remains; OCR is used only to decide whether the target is still readable in rendered pixels.
A form is flattened before redaction so a retained form stream cannot be hidden behind a page-level cover; visual checking supplements saved-byte removal.
Annotations are renderer-policy-sensitive, so appearance and carrier removal are checked separately; a reference disagreement is not accepted as a harmless tone difference.

rows.carrier: raster scan with invisible OCR overlay
rows.adjudication: The image ink and invisible searchable layer are distinct carriers; deleting either alone is insufficient and the untouched raster block must remain inked.
Filter support is security-sensitive: uneditable image pixels are conservatively removed rather than covered, while region-editable pixels preserve unrelated image content.
Mask and clipping differences are judged as content/geometry evidence, not raw pixel tone; two non-Excise renderers prevent electing a single outlier.
A box shifted by page rotation is a visible-leak failure even when a black rectangle appears elsewhere; target and neighbouring text are both required evidence.
Opacity is geometry and content evidence, not a tone threshold: a translucent cover that leaves a word OCR-readable is a visible-secret failure.
The baseline proves that a genuine glyph removal is blank in the region and preserves independent-renderer ink outside it; this separates removal from cosmetic coverage.
